summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes was admitted for nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea, found to be in mild diabetic ketoacidosis triggered by a viral gastroenteritis and bronchiolitis. She was treated with IV fluids and insulin, which resolved the DKA. An upper endoscopy showed mild esophagitis and gastric erythema likely from vomiting, with biopsies pending for H. pylori. She received a course of levofloxacin for bronchiolitis and was started on citalopram for anxiety and panic attacks. Her Lantus dose was reduced to 20 units at discharge to prevent hypoglycemia, and she was advised to follow up with her PCP for mental health and GI evaluation, including a possible gastric emptying study. She was discharged home in stable condition, tolerating oral intake, with instructions to monitor blood glucose and avoid narcotics.
